rationale: A wins because it keeps the story honest where the facts are thin. Its customer angle says, “the fact block says the manufacturer is ‘named’ as a customer but does not give the name,” which is exactly the adult move; B turns that same hole into “The Factory That Runs AI Without a Cloud Connection,” a headline the update does not support. B has useful bones, especially the benchmark scrutiny angle, but it keeps writing the story it wants instead of the story the facts permit.
gaps_in_A: “Hugging Face starts charging: a $50/seat enterprise tier on the open-source Hub” is defensible, but “starts charging” may overstate the fact set; the update says a paid enterprise tier is launching, not that Hugging Face had no prior paid enterprise products.
The on-device angle could ask for the exact model name earlier; without that, “a 1.8B model” is still slightly generic for the ML beat.

The customer-story angle is correctly caveated, but it is still a kept angle despite admitting “without it there is no customer story.” That probably belongs closer to conditional than ready-to-fit-check.
gaps_in_B: “Offline AI That Runs on a Laptop Is Now Good Enough for a Fortune 100 Factory” invents the core story. The facts say a Fortune 100 manufacturer is an early enterprise customer; they do not say it runs the offline model, runs it in a factory, or that it is “good enough” for real workloads.

“The Factory That Runs AI Without a Cloud Connection” is worse: it fabricates cloud-free factory deployment, plant-floor context, data-sovereignty rationale, and operational use cases from a single customer-citation fact.

“Enterprises Can Deploy This AI Without Owing Anyone a Subscription” fights the actual update, which includes a paid enterprise hub at $50/user/month. Apache 2.0 supports a licensing angle, but this headline turns an inference into a promise.
“the timing after reaching 2 million models” implies the 2M Hub figure is a fresh milestone tied to the tier launch. The update gives the number, not a date, growth rate, or threshold crossing.
